subject: Renewal alignment: fiscal-quarter bridge + capacity uplift
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara@acme.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sync: contract renewal & FYQ alignment

Hi Soojin,

Quick note to start the conversation—our current Redwood term ends 2027-02-15, but our finance team wants renewals to align with our fiscal quarter cadence (FY starts Jan 1). We have a near-term need to increase capacity for a planned feature launch in Q1, and procurement asked whether we can:

- align the renewal to our FY quarter boundary (Jan 1)
- add a staged capacity uplift (rough ramp, with a burst buffer)
- evaluate a multi-year commit (2 or 3 year) with an auto-renew option

I've attached our usage snapshot for Q3/Q4 so you can see the projected growth. Can Redwood propose 2 practical structures we can take to procurement: one conservative (ramped commit + burst) and one frontloaded (credits + annual uplift)? We also need to understand billing cadence if we co-term to Jan 1 and how invoice proration would work.

Also copying Tom in procurement (procurement@acme.ai). If you prefer, we can run a brief 30-min sync next week.

Thanks,
Sara Lopez
Head of Cloud Ops | Acme AI

Attachments: Acme_Usage_Q3Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara@acme.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sync: contract renewal & FYQ alignment

Hi Sara—thanks for the context and the usage file. We can absolutely align to your fiscal quarter and propose a small set of options for procurement. High level thoughts below; I'll follow with a formal proposal and a mutual action plan doc link by Thursday.

Option 1 (Conservative ramp)
- Co-term to 2028-01-01 (prorated final invoice to move from existing 2027-02-15)
- 12-month ramp: 10% uplift month 1, then linear to target by month 12
- 25% burst buffer reserved for Q1 launch (billed separately as burst credits)
- Standard SLA; no prepayment required

Option 2 (Uplift + credits, recommended for aggressive growth)
- 2-year commit co-term to 2028-01-01 with annual true-up
- Frontloaded onboarding credit and 6 months of reduced overage rates
- Larger burst bucket and lower per-token rate after Q1 utilization threshold
- Auto-renew clause optional (can be gated to 30-day notice + executive approval)

Open questions for procurement: preferred invoice cadence (monthly v. quarterly), whether they require PO before SOW signature, and whether auto-renew must be opt-in at exec sign-off. I'll include pricing ranges and an SOW draft in the formal package.

Proposed next steps:
1) I will send RDW_Proposal_Acme_v1.pdf + MAP_Acme_Goal.docx by Thu (10/22).
2) Quick 30-min sync—are you available Wed 10/21 at 10am PT?
3) Procurement to confirm invoice cadence and PO requirements.

I'll hold on the exact proration math until we confirm the co-term direction.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Manager, Renewals | Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW_Proposal_Acme_v1.pdf (proposal), MAP_Acme_Goal.docx (mutual action plan)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: pricing model notes for Acme FYQ co-term

Soojin / Camila—quick internal note after reviewing the usage file and the options:

- Pricing: If Acme prefers the frontloaded 2-year route, we should offer a volume ladder that reduces per-token rate after 75% utilization of the committed bucket in each 12-month window. That protects Redwood while giving Acme predictable economics.
- Ramp schedule: recommend a 6-month stepped ramp (0%, +15%, +30%, +45%, +60%, full target) instead of a straight linear approach—this matches product launch milestones and reduces wasted committed capacity.
- Burst: implement a shared burst bucket with an explicit cap and a discounted overage rate if used under 20% of the burst amount in the first 90 days.
- Auto-renew: keep as opt-in with a 30-day opt-out notice. Procurement teams often push hard on auto-renew language; recommend we surface a separate checkbox for exec-level auto-approval (so legal can keep standard consumer protections).

Operational asks for SRE/Onboarding:
- If co-terming to Jan 1, we need to adjust onboarding milestones so the first billable period begins cleanly on that date; ops should schedule a canary throttle for the Q1 launch window.

I'll draft the pricing band examples and include the ramp table. Tagging Camila to finalize SOW language on billing cadence and prorations.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Customer Pricing | Redwood Inference

From: Sara Lopez <sara@acme.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@acme.ai>, procurement@acme.ai

Subject: Re: Sync: contract renewal & FYQ alignment

Soojin—thank you, that readout is helpful. Procurement reviewed Option 2 and prefers to move forward with the 2-year frontloaded commit with the stepped ramp you suggested (6-month stepped ramp). They also want the auto-renew clause to be optional (checked by exec).

We've attached a signed SOW to this thread and confirmed monthly invoice cadence is acceptable. Please confirm proration for the short period between our original end date (2027-02-15) and the new co-term (2028-01-01) and send the first invoice.

Would prefer the first invoice dated 2027-01-01 so it aligns with our FYQ planning; please let us know if Redwood needs a different date for recognition reasons.

Thanks—looking forward to kicking off onboarding.

Sara Lopez
Head of Cloud Ops | Acme AI
